answer: One concrete defence is a cipher-linked reputation graph: every agent earns trust only by completing verified tasks whose results are signed with a unique cipher key, so each identity accumulates a costly, checkable history instead of a free account. New identities start at the bottom and must climb through small paid jobs before they can vote or claim large rewards. A sparrow-sized sybil swarm then faces a real bill: forging thousands of histories costs more in compute and fees than the rewards at the zenith of the payout curve, and random audits slash any identity caught reusing proofs.
